definitions.explanation: Stronger and more emotive than {汚|きたな}い — describes something so dirty or unkempt that it looks repellent. The らしい suffix adds a "gives off a ... impression" nuance.

examples.japanese: {汚|きたな}らしい⟦{格好|かっこう}→格好：01800_kakkou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He's dressed in a filthy, grimy way.

examples.japanese: ⟦{床|ゆか}→床：03652_yuka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{汚|きたな}らしくて⟦{座|すわ}れない→座る：00757_suwaru⟧。
examples.english: The floor is so grimy I can't sit down.

examples.japanese: {汚|きたな}らしい⟦{食|た}べ{方|かた}→食べ方：27437_tabekata⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{周|まわ}り→周り：01732_mawari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{不快|ふかい}→不快：11386_fukai⟧にさせる。
examples.english: Eating in a disgusting way makes those around you uncomfortable.

notes:
An intensified, more emotional form of ⟦{汚|きたな}い→汚い：00788_kitanai⟧ (dirty). The らしい here means "looking/seeming," so {汚|きたな}らしい stresses a repellent, unclean impression rather than mere dirtiness.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {汚|きたな}らしく
- Negative: {汚|きたな}らしく⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧
- Past: {汚|きたな}らしかった

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{汚|きたな}い→汚い：00788_kitanai⟧: dirty — plainer, less emotive
- ⟦むさ{苦|くる}しい→むさ苦しい：29821_musakurushii⟧: squalid, stuffy — filthy and cramped or shabby

forms.label: Conditional たら
forms.negative: {汚|きたな}らしくなかったら
